name: Trapping_factors_of_semiprimes_as_braids_within_Wild_Arcs

phase_0.boundary_condition: The wild arc's limit set — a fractal topological boundary that losslessly encodes the bulk braid structure and prevents factor escape without global restructuring of the embedding space.

⊢.justification: The void state before any braid embedding exists; the semiprime n = p×q sits as an undifferentiated integer with latent factor structure.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor that closes the system; the fractal boundary of the wild arc contains the full braid information losslessly (scale-collapse topology) and defines the topological container.

≻.justification: Forward morphism that weaves prime factors p and q into a braid within the wild arc; directed transformation from arithmetic factors to topological strands.

≺.justification: Contravariant descent that reads the braid invariant to recover prime factors; reverse transformation from topological encoding back to arithmetic factors.

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of braid generators (σ_i) and Reidemeister moves; composes elementary crossings into the full braid word representing the factor pair.

⊙.justification: Identity operation where the braid recognizes its own isotopy class; the knot invariant (Jones/Alexander polynomial) acts as self-model confirming the encoding.

∈.justification: Splits the computational path into two arms: T-arm where the braid invariant successfully distinguishes p and q (factorized), F-arm where the invariant fails to separate them (unfactorized).

∋.justification: Rejoins the factorized and unfactorized arms by union of their topological data; conflicting outcomes (success and failure) fuse to B-state representing the critical phase transition.

⊤.justification: Affirmative arm where the braid group representation yields distinct eigenvalues for p and q; the topological invariant constructively proves factorization.

⊥.justification: Negative arm where the braid invariant collapses (degenerate eigenvalues) and cannot distinguish the factors; constructive refutation of factorizability via this embedding.

⊞.justification: Paradice state at the factorization threshold where both factorized and unfactorized configurations are held simultaneously; the scale-free correlation length diverges (ξ → ∞).

⊡.justification: ROM fixation of the extracted prime factors; the factorization result becomes an irreversible measurement record appended to the topological log.

phase_2.split_input: braid-encoded semiprime at critical embedding depth
split_outputs: factorized arm (EVALT/⊤) — braid invariant separates p and q
phase_2.fuse_result: critical superposition (ENGAGR/⊞) — both factorization outcomes held as B-state at the phase transition
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Semiprime before wild arc embedding — no braid structure, no factor information accessible, register 00.
phase_3.true_description: Factorization constructively proven — braid invariant yields distinct prime factors p and q, register 01.
phase_3.false_description: Factorization constructively refuted — braid invariant degenerates, factors remain trapped but indistinguishable, register 10.
phase_3.both_description: Critical superposition — factorized and unfactorized states held simultaneously at the scale-free threshold; the braid encoding sits at the exact boundary where μ∘δ = id and ξ → ∞, register 11.

phase_5.memory_mechanism: Topological log in the wild arc's fractal boundary — the limit set stores the braid isotopy class as a scale-free holographic record; IFIX operations append permanent entries to this boundary log; the register state is the current braid invariant evaluation.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Criticality-driven phase clock — operations advance at the factorization threshold (ξ → ∞); the Frobenius condition μ∘δ = id governs timing; metastable locking (τ = ∞) prevents premature equilibration; the scheduler is the braid group's own representation theory.
